name: Drakes Bay
say: The anchorage inside Chimney Rock, sheltered from the north-west by Point Reyes. White cliffs, and room for a fleet. Open to the south.

ashore.name: the beach under the white cliffs
ashore.say: A walk on the sand where Drake may have careened the Golden Hinde in 1579. Elephant seals have the far end.

name: Bolinas
say: Anchor off in the bay: the lagoon entrance is a shifting sand bar for small boats at high water only. Duxbury Reef breaks the north-west swell.

ashore.name: the saloon on Wharf Road
ashore.say: The oldest bar in the county, if you can find the town: the locals take the road signs down.

name: Spud Point Marina
say: The fishing fleet's marina on the west side of Bodega Harbour, a mile up the dredged channel. Keep between the marks: it is mud both sides.

ashore.name: Spud Point Crab Company
ashore.say: Crab sandwiches and chowder across the road from the docks, eaten at a picnic table with the fleet in view.

name: Bodega Bay wharf
say: The town side of the harbour, at the head of the channel. Hitchcock filmed The Birds along this waterfront.

ashore.name: The Tides Wharf
ashore.say: A window table over the harbour, sea lions under the fish dock, and gulls that have seen the film.

name: Pillar Point Harbor
say: Inside the outer breakwater at Half Moon Bay: the only harbour between the Gate and Santa Cruz. Enter round the reef buoys, never across the reef. Mavericks breaks just outside in winter.

ashore.name: the brewery on the harbour at Princeton
ashore.say: A fire pit, a pint and fish tacos, with the boats at anchor a stone's throw off.

name: Johnson Pier
say: The fish pier in the inner harbour at Pillar Point, where the boats sell salmon and crab off the stern.

ashore.name: the fish shack at the head of the pier
ashore.say: Fish and chips in paper, straight off the boats.

name: Pacifica Pier
say: A quarter-mile fishing pier on an open beach. Anchor off it in settled weather only: there is no shelter and the surf is heavy.

ashore.name: the cafe at the foot of the pier
ashore.say: Coffee and a crab roll while the anglers pull salmon and stripers over the rail.

name: Fisherman Bay
say: The dent in the north side of Southeast Farallon. Deep, rocky and open: a place to lie for an hour and look. It is a wildlife refuge and nobody lands.

name: Horseshoe Cove
say: The little harbour under the north end of the bridge. The last stop before the ocean and the first after it.

ashore.name: the yacht club at Fort Baker
ashore.say: A beer on the deck under the bridge, watching who comes in over the bar.
